trials.name: A4 Study
trials.population: Cognitively normal older adults with preclinical Alzheimer's disease (amyloid positive on PET)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline to week 240 in the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC) score
trials.results_summary: The trial failed to meet its primary endpoint; solanezumab did not slow cognitive decline compared to placebo. Blood samples collected during screening were retrospectively analyzed to validate biomarkers like p-tau217.

trials.name: BioFINDER-2
trials.drug: Diagnostic Test: Elecsys / Lumipulse (Abeta42, Ttau, Ptau)
trials.population: Cognitively healthy adults, individuals with subjective cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, AD dementia, and other dementias
trials.primary_endpoint: Clinical diagnosis according to consensus group decision blinded to the diagnostic test
trials.results_summary: As an ongoing observational cohort, formal completion is years away, but multiple interim analyses have robustly demonstrated plasma p-tau217's high accuracy in detecting amyloid and tau pathology.

related_evidence.description: Primary results of the Phase 3 A4 Study showing solanezumab failed to slow cognitive decline in preclinical AD.
Prospective cohort study from BioFINDER integrating plasma p-tau217 for AD diagnosis and stratification.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence strongly supports the document's central claim regarding the high diagnostic accuracy of plasma p-tau217. Observational cohorts like BioFINDER-2 have robustly replicated its superiority over other plasma markers for identifying Alzheimer's pathology. However, prospective interventional trials evaluating p-tau217 as a standalone diagnostic endpoint for primary care implementation remain sparse, leaving a gap between retrospective validation and real-world utility. Furthermore, a major contextual discrepancy exists in how the A4 trial is framed: the document uses its retrospective screening data to model cost reductions, but A4 itself was a failed Phase 3 therapeutic trial for solanezumab, not a diagnostic trial. Finally, the heavy financial conflicts of interest among the authors—including patents and equity in the discussed diagnostic tools—necessitate cautious interpretation of their highly optimistic timelines for clinical rollout.
discrepancies: The document cites the A4 trial to model how blood tests reduce confirmatory PET/CSF prescreening requirements. However, the registry record (NCT02008357) shows A4 was a therapeutic trial for an anti-amyloid drug (solanezumab) that failed its primary cognitive endpoint, not a prospective trial evaluating biomarkers. The document relies entirely on retrospective analysis of A4's screening cohort to validate the biomarker utility.
